results.title: Rethinking the Ghanaian compound house: Co-living as part of the housing solution
results.content: When we discuss Ghana’s housing challenges, the conversation often turns to acquiring more land, building new estates, and finding the money to finance construction. These are important. But I believe another question deserves attention: What can we do with the buildings we have already started? There are unfinished properties that could potentially provide accommodation if they were completed and put to productive use. At the same time, there are people who need somewhere decent to live but cannot afford an entire house or a self-contained apartment. Could co-living help bring these two needs together? I believe it is worth exploring—not as a complete answer to Ghana’s housing crisis, but as a practical alternative that could provide accommodation, create investment opportunities, and unlock some of the capital tied up in unfinished buildings. results.title: Obuasi Trade Show 2026 to bring businesses together for four-day exhibition in December
results.content: The 2026 Obuasi Trade Show is scheduled to take place from December 21 to 24 at the Obuasi Black Park, bringing together businesses, entrepreneurs, manufacturers and traders from across the Ashanti Region. The four-day exhibition is expected to provide a platform for businesses to showcase their products and services, connect with potential partners and investors, and explore opportunities to access new markets. The initiative is being spearheaded by the Obuasi Trade Show Consortium, with AngloGold Ashanti Obuasi Mine as headline sponsor. It forms part of the Mine’s 10-year Socio-Economic Development Plan (SEDP 2022–2031), which seeks to promote local entrepreneurship, expand opportunities for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and support efforts to diversify Obuasi’s economy beyond mining.

results.title: NAIMOS arrests 30 suspects, intercepts 35 trucks in Ketu North sand-winning operation
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has arrested 30 people and intercepted 35 tipper trucks in a crackdown on suspected illegal sand-winning activities in the Ketu North Municipality of the Volta Region. The operation, conducted on November 13 with support from the Ghana Army’s Artillery Brigade, targeted two sites at Agbozume Klikor and Ohawu, where task force personnel disrupted active sand-winning activities. According to NAIMOS, a significant number of the intercepted trucks bore Togolese registration numbers, raising concerns about the movement of vehicles involved in sand extraction in the area. The 30 suspects were handed over to the Dzodze District Police Station for further investigations, while the 35 trucks were moved to a secure holding location.

results.title: NAIMOS arrests 23 suspected illegal miners, destroys 33 changfan machines in Tarkwa crackdown
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has arrested 23 suspected illegal miners and destroyed 33 changfan machines and 47 water pumps in a two-day crackdown on illegal mining along the Tarkwa road corridor in the Western Region. The operations, conducted on November 12 and 13, targeted mining activities taking place close to roads and surrounding communities within the Tarkwa-Nsuaem Municipality. The enforcement exercise covered communities stretching from Nsuaem and Simpa to Dompim and Bonsa, where task force personnel encountered several illegal mining sites. On the first day, operations between Nsuaem and Simpa resulted in the destruction of 15 changfan machines and 22 water pumps.

results.title: Linda Ocloo blames persistent Accra streetlight outages on cable theft
results.content: Greater Accra Regional Minister Linda Ocloo has blamed persistent streetlight outages in parts of Accra on the theft of cables and other components, saying the problem is undermining efforts to improve public lighting across the capital. She said some installations become dysfunctional barely two weeks after repairs because unidentified persons return to steal components, making it difficult to sustain improvements. Speaking to JoyNews’ Stephen Mensah on the sidelines of the NDC Greater Accra Regional elections, Mrs Ocloo rejected suggestions that the Regional Coordinating Council had failed to act, insisting it had fulfilled its commitment to illuminate identified areas. “We have a promise and we did the lighting. You are witness. The media was present. We went around. The places that we told you there has been lighting, you went around and saw it physically,” she said.
